sources.snippet: Radio surveys record millions of candidate signals, but only about 9% are real pulsars — the rest is noise and radio frequency interference. Manually checking each candidate doesn't scale, which makes this a natural machine learning problem: can a model reliably tell real pulsars apart from noise?
